newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa set for three rate cuts in 1997 - Syfrets.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa set for three rate cuts in 1997 - Syfrets.

text.p: South Africa can expect three interest rate cuts of one percentage point each during 1997, according to Sandra Gordon, chief economist at fund management company Syfrets.
"The first cut is anticipated during the first quarter of 1997, the second around mid-year and the third during the final quarter of next year," she said in an economic review.
Each cut in the Reserve Bank's key Bank rate would be accompanied by a similar reduction in prime rate. The Bank rate currently stands at 16 percent and prime at 19.25 percent.
Gordon said the easing in rates had been delayed until next year due to the Reserve Bank's concerns about balance of payments.
But the current account deficit was likely to narrow sharply during the next 18 months reflecting slowing consumer demand and investment, and an improvement in export earnings.
In addition, an expected resumption in capital inflows resulting from some progress with privatisation plans should ease pressure further on the balance of payments in the year ahead.
